subject: POC gate rollout — API keys / org seed / allowlist / VPC peering timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@pilothealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-30T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: POC gate rollout: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering — next steps

Neha — thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have internal buy-in to run a production-like POC with Redwood; legal and infra asked for a short mutual action plan they can track against.

Top asks from our side to get to a meaningful evaluation this quarter:
- Org seed & admin invite so our engineers can create a tenant and run basic inference tests
- Short-lived API keys for staging + a plan for rotating to long-lived keys if we move to Dedicated
- IP allowlist values and any public endpoints for egress/ingress (we will add on our firewall)
- VPC peering feasibility and requirements (peering window, CIDR, who owns peering request)

We can be flexible, but need these items in a MAP to share with our CISO and procurement. Can you share Redwood’s recommended timeline (2–3 week target preferred) and a small checklist we can attach to the MAP?

Also looping Alex (network) and our procurement lead.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Integrations | PilotHealth
attachments: pilot-initial-scope.pdf (referenced)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-30T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC gate rollout: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering — next steps

Sarah — great to hear. I’ve sketched a compact MAP and proposed dates below; attaching a short milestone sheet and our setup playbook for your infra team. Please treat the dates as target windows — we’ll lock them after we have your firewall CIDRs and Alex’s peering contact.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Org seed + admin invite (Day 0–1): Redwood creates PilotHealth tenant; invite two admin users.
2) API keys (Day 1–3): Issue ephemeral staging keys + instructions for rotating; CS will provision a scoped key for your test suite.
3) IP allowlist (Day 2–5): You share allowlist; Redwood confirms required endpoints and public IPs.
4) VPC peering (Day 7–14): Coordinate peering window; network teams exchange CIDRs and route tables.
5) Validation & runbook (Day 10–21): Smoke tests, perf run, token-cost snapshot, and handoff to success team.

Attachments: Neha_MAP_MilestoneSheet.xlsx, redwood-poc-setup-playbook.pdf (playbook has sample terraform snippets and peering checklist).

Action items for PilotHealth: share firewall contact, preferred admin emails for org seed, and CIDRs you can allow in the short term. We can hit a Dec 8–12 peering window if that works on your end.

I’ll loop Ben to outline the network requirements.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Lead, Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0193

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-01T08:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC gate rollout: API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering — network prep

Sarah / Neha — quick network note from infra:

What Redwood needs from PilotHealth to schedule peering and allowlist traffic:
- Source CIDR(s) PilotHealth will use for peering (we prefer a /24 or larger for peering; if you have multiple ranges, list all)
- Firewall contact for download/upload testing (Alex or network L3)
- Expected traffic pattern during test (egress tokens/sec, average seq length) — helps us size ephemeral capacity
- Which AWS account / VPC you want to peer (we can provide account id and suggested route table entries)

We will:
- Provide a minimal set of public IPs and FQDNs you need to allow for the hosted API endpoints
- Share a short peer-prep-checklist for your cloud team to run prior to the peering window

Proposed peering window: Dec 8–10 (UTC-aware scheduling available). If PilotHealth needs earlier, we can try Dec 3–5 but will prioritize teams with earlier commit dates.

Attaching: peer-prep-checklist.txt (small checklist).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pilothealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@pilothealth.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC gate rollout: PilotHealth allowlist + peering contact

Ben / Neha — Alex here (network). Thanks for the clear checklist. See the initial allowlist attached (PilotHealth_Allowlist_v1.csv) — it contains our outbound NAT ranges and the staging VPC CIDRs we can open for a peering test.

Short answers to Ben’s questions:
- CIDRs we can offer for peering: 10.40.32.0/24 and 10.40.33.0/24
- Firewall contact: myself (alex.turner@pilothealth.com) and our security engineer Priya Shah (priya.shah@pilothealth.com)
- Traffic expectation: small burst (2–5 r/s) during smoke tests; heavier runs possible on Day 14 for perf tests (~50 r/s sustained short bursts)

We do need a SOC2 addendum recorded in the MAP before we exchange certain artifacts; procurement will push on that. Happy to sign a short addendum — share your standard wording and we’ll fast-track.

Alex Turner
Network Lead | PilotHealth
attachments: PilotHealth_Allowlist_v1.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pilothealth.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@pilothealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-02T16:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC gate rollout: API keys / org seed / allowlist / peering timeline — confirmed

Thanks Alex — this is perfect. Summary & next steps so we have a single source of truth for the MAP: 

Summary:
- Org seed: Redwood will create PilotHealth tenant and invite neha-testing@pilothealth.com and infra-admin@pilothealth.com by EOD Dec 3.
- API keys: CS will provision a scoped staging key (rotatable) by Dec 4; we’ll send instructions for rotating and for scoped-permissions.
- IP allowlist: We confirm receipt of PilotHealth_Allowlist_v1.csv (10.40.32.0/24, 10.40.33.0/24 + NAT ranges). Redwood will publish required public egress IPs and FQDNs by Dec 3.
- VPC peering: Target window Dec 8–10; Ben will coordinate the exact time with Alex. Please confirm the AWS account ID and VPC ID you want to peer to by Dec 4.
- Compliance: We’ll attach a short SOC2 addendum to the MAP and route to your procurement — Marissa will own that doc from our side.

Operational links: HubSpot deal DL-2025-0893 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765), DocuSign signature packet (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/placeholder-signature/DL-2025-0893).

Action items:
- PilotHealth: confirm peering VPC ID + provide procurement contact (for SOC2 addendum) by Dec 4.
- Redwood: create tenant and provision staging key by Dec 4; publish allowlist endpoints by Dec 3.
- Both teams: schedule a short network coordination call (30m) Dec 5–6; Ben to propose times.

Marissa, I’ve asked you to prepare the SOC2 addendum and the DocuSign wrapper — please draft and I’ll route.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Lead, Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
